dct_description_sm: The primary goal of this project is to explore methods to disseminate the work of northern researchers to northern communities. The results will be useful in better understanding effective methods in disseminating the research of northern researchers and networks.  The research contributes to the literature linking northern research with northern education and develops strategies to support more meaningful exchanges between northern residents and researchers as part of the research and learning process. As a case study, this project explored how to disseminate the research of two research networks: (i) PPS Arctic Canada, a national network (part of an international network) that is investigating the impacts of a changing climate on northern vegetation at the treeline; and (ii) Environmental Change and Traditional Use of the Old Crow Flats, a community-driven IPY project that investigates the Gwich'in traditional territory.
